title.en: Types of banks and their functions

body.en: Banks are commercial banks (public and private sector), cooperative banks, specialised banks such as NABARD, SIDBI and EXIM Bank, and the central bank, the RBI. Commercial banks accept deposits in current, savings and fixed accounts, lend through loans, cash credit, overdraft and discounting of bills, provide cheque facility, remit funds through drafts and pay orders, and offer allied services such as lockers and bill payment.

points.en: Commercial, cooperative, specialised and central banks
Lending: loans, cash credit, overdraft, discounting

narration.en: Banks are commercial banks (public and private sector), cooperative banks, specialised banks such as NABARD, SIDBI and EXIM Bank, and the central bank, the RBI. Commercial banks accept deposits in current, savings and fixed accounts, lend through loans, cash credit, overdraft and discounting of bills, provide cheque facility, remit funds through drafts and pay orders, and offer allied services such as lockers and bill payment.
narration.kn: ಬ್ಯಾಂಕುಗಳು ವಾಣಿಜ್ಯ, ಸಹಕಾರಿ, ವಿಶೇಷ ಮತ್ತು ಕೇಂದ್ರ ಬ್ಯಾಂಕುಗಳು. ವಾಣಿಜ್ಯ ಬ್ಯಾಂಕುಗಳು ಠೇವಣಿ ಸ್ವೀಕರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ, ಸಾಲ ನೀಡುತ್ತವೆ, ಹಣ ವರ್ಗಾಯಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: E-banking means banking through the internet and electronic channels. It includes electronic fund transfer through NEFT and RTGS, ATMs, debit and credit cards, point-of-sale terminals and mobile banking. It allows banking 24 × 7, gives instant transactions, frees customers from carrying cash, encourages financial discipline and reduces the load on branches.

points.en: ATM, debit card, credit card, POS
Benefits: 24 × 7, instant, no cash needed, less load on branches

narration.kn: ಇ-ಬ್ಯಾಂಕಿಂಗ್ ಎಂದರೆ ಇಂಟರ್ನೆಟ್ ಮತ್ತು ವಿದ್ಯುನ್ಮಾನ ಮಾರ್ಗಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಬ್ಯಾಂಕಿಂಗ್. ಇದು ದಿನದ 24 ಗಂಟೆ ಲಭ್ಯ ಮತ್ತು ನಗದು ಹೊತ್ತೊಯ್ಯುವ ಅಗತ್ಯ ತಪ್ಪಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: A trader has ₹40,000 in his current account and an overdraft limit of ₹1,00,000. He issues a cheque for ₹1,10,000. (a) Will it be honoured? (b) How much is overdrawn? (c) Should he use NEFT or RTGS to send ₹1,10,000 instead?

steps.en: (a) Maximum he can draw = ₹40,000 + ₹1,00,000 = ₹1,40,000, so the ₹1,10,000 cheque is honoured.
(b) Overdrawn amount = ₹1,10,000 − ₹40,000 = ₹70,000, on which interest is charged.
(c) ₹1,10,000 is below the RTGS minimum of ₹2,00,000, so he must use NEFT.
